messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED — KV_CACHE_REUSE_CORRUPTION. Alert from runtime-health: sudden rise in seq_offset_mismatch and cross-request key reuse anomalies. Pager to oncall.

alice (oncall): getting user reports: snippets appearing from prior sessions inserted into unrelated responses. Also seeing a latency spike on batch-heavy routes. Acknowledge.

ben (sre): digging into logs. Pattern: when continuous batching + kv_cache_reuse enabled, there are cases where cache entries are reused across requests with non-overlapping gen_ids. Count ~5.9% of requests on affected pools (us-central1-gpu-3 / eu-west1-gpu-5). Stacktraces point to reuse_dispatcher path.

carla (eng-runtime): reproducer: run throughput harnesser with variable seq lengths and eviction pressure. Observed cache entries carrying prior seq_start/seq_end but applied to later requests — stale KV slices. Likely root: race between cache eviction callback and reuse index update.

darren (eng-ml): that will corrupt attention KV; downstream outputs will have blended context. Customer impact severity: high for long-prefix use cases. Any enterprise customers impacted?

emily (cs): yes — two paid customers reported corrupted outputs; one (fintech-partner) paused traffic. CS needs an interim message. What's the fastest mitigation?

alice (oncall): options: 1) flip runtime flag to disable kv reuse, 2) throttle continuous batching, 3) deploy code-level hotfix. Which is fastest and lowest risk?

ben (sre): fastest is toggle runtime flag off per-region. No code change. Downside: higher CPU/GPU token cost and latency. Estimated error drop immediate after worker restarts.

carla (eng-runtime): agree. We should also add emergency per-worker invalidation hook so we can avoid full-region restarts. Plan: set kv_cache_reuse=false, then trigger rolling drain/restart of reuse-capable workers. I'll prepare backport for a safety guard: validate cache.gen_id == request.gen_id before reuse.

alice (oncall): ben start the rollout. Notify CS and PM.

ben (sre): running command on us-central1 now:

```
infractl set-flag --region=us-central1 kv_cache_reuse=false
infractl rolling-restart --pool=reuse-pool-7 --batch=3 --wait=180s
```

deploy-bot: acknowledged, rolling restart started on pool reuse-pool-7.

opsbot: reaction :white_check_mark:

carla (eng-runtime): quick patch we should land: attach generation_id and seq_start to cache metadata and check offsets before reusing. Also on mismatch, emit metric and fallback to fresh kv. Patch minimal, low-risk.

darren (eng-ml): add runtime unit tests that simulate mixed seq_start sequences and eviction in the middle of reuse. I'll produce tests in the next hour.

emily (cs): messaging to customers: "We detected a caching bug that could cause parts of unrelated requests to appear in completions. We have temporarily disabled the cache optimization and are rolling a validated fix. No evidence of data exfiltration. We'll update you in 2 hours." Sending now.

ben (sre): us-central1 batch 1 restarted. Error rate in that region dropped from 6% -> 0.4% in ~7 minutes. Proceeding to eu-west1.

carla (eng-runtime): building hotfix PR: changes are annotation of cache entries and guard clause before reuse. Code snippet:

```
// reuse guard
if (entry.gen_id != req.gen_id || req.seq_start < entry.seq_start) {
  metrics.incr("reuse_guard_blocked");
  fetch_fresh_kv();
} else {
  apply_kv(entry, offset=req.seq_start - entry.seq_start);
}
```

alice (oncall): proposed rollout for hotfix: canary on a non-critical pool at 5% for 20m, validate metrics, then ramp. Keep runtime flag off until backports are in.

carla (eng-runtime): hotfix build green. Canary deploy to us-central1-pool-9 at 5% traffic.

darren (eng-ml): added unit + e2e tests for boundary cases. CI passes locally.

ben (sre): canary metrics 25m: zero reuse_guard_blocked anomalies, no seq_offset_mismatch logs, latency comparable with reuse-off baseline (+6% p95). Rolling hotfix out to all pools but keeping runtime flag off for safety.

emily (cs): customers acknowledged interim update; fintech-partner resumed limited traffic after mitigation. Monitoring closely.

jorge (pm): capturing follow-ups: 1) backport to LTS (carla), 2) add metric and alert for reuse_guard_blocked spikes (ben), 3) write postmortem and customer timeline (alice/emily), 4) add chaos test in staging to simulate eviction races (darren). ETA for postmortem: 72 hours.

alice (oncall): handing to next oncall in 30m; incident remains mitigated (runtime flag off, hotfix ready/backported). Great job triaging quickly. :heart:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — KV_CACHE_REUSE_CORRUPTION. Mitigation: runtime flag disabled, hotfix implemented and canaried. Follow-ups scheduled.
